label: ex-positive-derivative-at-zero-with-no-local-monotonicity

VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: F is defined on all of ℝ. The derivative F'(0)=1 exists via the boundedness of ψ, and F is differentiable for x≠0 by standard calculus rules. Any punctured neighbourhood of 0 contains reciprocal sequences where ψ'>2 (hence F' eventually negative) and where ψ'<−2 (hence F' eventually positive). Thus no neighbourhood can have a constant derivative sign; the contradiction with L2 stands. No degenerate, empty, or endpoint special case alters the reasoning.

SOURCES: All five cited items were inspected in full. ex-piecewise-polynomial-periodic-oscillator supplies a bounded C¹ periodic ψ with derivative values 3 and −3 (thus >2 and <−2) in every period. thm-algebra-of-derivatives and thm-chain-rule correctly justify the differentiation of F for x≠0. def-derivative provides the definition used in the limit at 0 and the derivative sign inference. def-monotone-function gives the global monotonicity definition that L2 summarizes. Every dependency is exactly matched to its usage.

CHECKED: The title, the full public statement (“There is a differentiable function F with F'(0)>0 that is not monotone on any neighbourhood of 0”), Facts & Assumptions, and each numbered step (1.1, 1.2, 2.1) were examined. No Remarks section exists. The proof is logically sound, the witness is correctly constructed, and the contradiction is valid.
